claim.why_it_matters: In the left column above the D heading and in the whole right column, every index line has the same indentation, so the parent/child structure is lost. The lines under the D heading are indented correctly.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 842 (PDF p864) is a two-column index. Sub-entries are visibly indented under their headwords: ADD statement..SUBTRACT statement under the continued heading, UNSTRING statement 545 under COUNT IN phrase, ACCEPT MESSAGE COUNT statement 667 under COUNT phrase, SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph 194 under CRT STATUS / CURRENCY SIGN / CURSOR clause, EXIT statement 446 under CYCLE phrase; in the right column Definintion 365 (continuing Data-pointer), INITIALIZE statement 457, ACCEPT statement 409, TYPE clause 354, Alignment 389 under Decimal point, USE statement 549, Normal completion 392, and the DEPENDING ON / DESCENDING KEY sub-entries. In the markdown every one of those lines sits at the same three-space indent as its headword (e.g. '   COUNT IN phrase\' then '   UNSTRING statement 545\'), while the block under the D heading uses   for sub-entries correctly. The claim quotes both sources accurately. The loss changes what the index says: 'Alignment 389' and 'Definintion 365' read as top-level index terms rather than sub-entries of 'Decimal point' and 'Data-pointer', and 'UNSTRING statement 545' reads as its own term. Index content is non-normative, so this does not affect compiler semantics, but it is a genuine structural discrepancy, not mere whitespace.
